$comment: Hand-maintained. One entry per skill folder in ../.claude/skills/. Fields: group (one of `groups`), summary (one plain-English line), whenToUse (one or two sentences for newcomers), deps (skill folder names this skill calls; followed transitively by the installer), optional commands [{cmd, desc}] to override what is extracted from SKILL.md. Skills missing from this file still appear under group "Other". The build fails if a dep is not a real skill folder.

feature-loop.summary: Turns a rough feature brief into a spec, working code, a verified result, and lessons learned, in six stages.
feature-loop.whenToUse: You have a feature idea or a product document and want Claude to plan it, build it, and check it against the plan. Drop the brief in .claude/specs/inbox/ and run it.

commands.desc: Run end to end without stopping for approval
Use a document from anywhere as the brief
Accept the proposed split of a multi-feature document
Approve the brainstorm and continue to the spec
Send the brainstorm back with feedback
Skip planning and build from an existing spec
Only check the current changes against the spec
Preview the skill updates without applying them
Limit how many helper agents run at the same time
Run the checks one after another instead of in parallel

figma-to-code.summary: Turns a Figma link or node into React Native + NativeWind components.
figma-to-code.whenToUse: You have a Figma URL (or node id) for a screen and want matching React Native code.

figma-to-code-skill.summary: The full Figma to React Native playbook: flexbox layout, design tokens first, reusable components.
figma-to-code-skill.whenToUse: You are turning any design (link, screenshot, or description) into React Native UI and want clean, reusable layout code.

react-native-optimization-and-architectu.summary: React Native and Expo best practices: list performance, animations, navigation, native modules.
react-native-optimization-and-architectu.whenToUse: You are building or speeding up a React Native / Expo app and want Claude to follow proven performance rules.

quality-assurance.summary: Runs the compile gate (lint, types, tests, contract and null checks) and lets Claude fix failures up to 3 times.
quality-assurance.whenToUse: You want one command that checks the build is green and, if not, feeds the error back so Claude can fix it.

pre-merge-check.summary: Runs lint, type checks, and tests in parallel (TS/JS and Python) and stops if anything fails.
pre-merge-check.whenToUse: Before you open or merge a pull request, to make sure nothing is broken.

feature-qa.summary: Tests a feature end to end on its own: writes a feature doc, designs test cases, writes and runs Playwright tests, triages failures, and hands back a report with a verdict.
feature-qa.whenToUse: When a feature is built and you want proof it actually works in a real browser or app, without babysitting the testing.

null-safety-scan.summary: Finds places where code could crash on a missing value (null, undefined, None).
null-safety-scan.whenToUse: Before merging logic that reads data from APIs, forms, or optional fields.

complexity-check.summary: Flags functions and files that are too long, too nested, or too complex.
complexity-check.whenToUse: As a merge gate, or when a function feels hard to follow and you want a second opinion.

test-coverage-delta.summary: Shows only the new lines in your change that no test covers.
test-coverage-delta.whenToUse: You want to know whether a pull request is actually tested, without wading through the whole project's coverage.

dead-code-scan.summary: Finds unused exports, unreachable code, and orphan files.
dead-code-scan.whenToUse: Before a cleanup or big refactor, to see what can safely go.

perf-budget.summary: Tracks bundle size, API latency, and app startup time against a baseline and blocks regressions.
perf-budget.whenToUse: Before merging changes that could make the app bigger or slower.

contract-drift-check.summary: Catches fields that were renamed, removed, or made required on one side of the frontend / backend / AI boundary only.
contract-drift-check.whenToUse: After changing shared types, DTOs, or API schemas, to make sure every service still agrees.

api-mock-parity.summary: Checks that your mock data and fixtures still match the real API.
api-mock-parity.whenToUse: After a backend response shape changes, so the app is not quietly tested against stale mocks.

migration-safety.summary: Flags risky database migrations: data loss, table locks, unsafe backfills.
migration-safety.whenToUse: Before merging any change that touches database migrations or the schema.

dependency-hygiene.summary: Finds unused packages, duplicate versions, peer conflicts, and license problems.
dependency-hygiene.whenToUse: Before a release or a dependency upgrade, or when node_modules feels too big.

security-audit.summary: A 42-rule OWASP security check, single-rule deep dives, API over-sharing audit, and a full pen-test report.
security-audit.whenToUse: Before opening a PR or shipping a release, or whenever you want to know what is left to fix on security.

security-scan.summary: Scans your staged changes for leaked secrets and known-vulnerable packages.
security-scan.whenToUse: Right before you commit, so passwords and API keys never reach the repo.

pentesting.summary: Thinks like an attacker: maps your attack surface, finds exploitable paths, and can apply fixes with your permission.
pentesting.whenToUse: After a meaningful change that nobody has looked at from an attacker's point of view.

feature-review.summary: Gives a merge verdict on someone else's PR: what could break, how the approach compares, and which tests are missing.
feature-review.whenToUse: You are reviewing a teammate's branch or PR and want a structured, team-lead-level review.

feature-audit.summary: Runs every relevant review skill on a feature in parallel and gives one merge verdict.
feature-audit.whenToUse: At the end of the day, to audit a feature, PR, or branch with everything at once. Works well as a nightly review.

system-design.summary: Audits how your app, backend, and AI service fit together: race conditions, contracts, and production readiness.
system-design.whenToUse: You want a design opinion on a feature, route, or screen, especially before it goes to production.

adr-writer.summary: Writes a one-page Architecture Decision Record to docs/adr/ when you add a library or pattern.
adr-writer.whenToUse: You are adding a new dependency or architectural pattern and want the reasoning written down.

git-push.summary: Reviews your staged files, writes a clear commit message, asks you to confirm, then commits and pushes.
git-push.whenToUse: You have staged your changes and want a safe, well-described commit pushed in one step.

pr-open.summary: Opens a GitHub pull request with the title, summary, and test plan filled in from your changes.
pr-open.whenToUse: Your branch is ready and you want a PR opened without writing the description by hand.

generate-docs.summary: Writes readable feature documentation from your recent changes into docs/features/.
generate-docs.whenToUse: A feature just landed and you want docs for it without starting from a blank page.

team-pulse.summary: A daily or weekly digest of commits, PRs, and reviews across your team's repos.
team-pulse.whenToUse: You lead a team and want a quick written summary of who shipped what. Needs a .claude/team.yaml file.
